# Install the package ggplot2

```{r}
# install.packages("ggplot2")
```

# Load the package ggplot2

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```

# Specify the dataset

```{r}
ggplot(cars)
```

# Specify aesthetics

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + aes(x=speed, y=dist)
```

# Specify a geom layer

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + aes(x=speed, y=dist) + geom_point()
```

# Add a trend line

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + aes(x=speed, y=dist) + geom_point() + geom_smooth()
```

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + aes(x=speed, y=dist) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method="lm")
```

# Add labels and theme

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + aes(x=speed, y=dist) + geom_point() + labs(title="Speed and Stopping Distance of Cars", x="Speed (MPH)", y="Stopping Distance (ft)") + geom_smooth(method="lm", se=FALSE) + theme_bw()
```

# Read in our drug expression data

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

# Use the nrow() function to find how many genes are in this dataset

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

# Use the colnames() function and the n(col) function to find out what the column names are and how many columns there are

```{r}
colnames(genes)
ncol(genes)
```

# Use the table() function on the state column to find out how many 'up' regulated genes there are

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

# What fraction of total genes is up-regulated?

```{r}
round(table(genes$State)/nrow(genes)*100, 2)
```

# Plot the dataset

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2) + geom_point()
```

# Add color

```{r}
p <- ggplot(genes) + aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) + geom_point()
p
```

```{r}
p + scale_colour_manual(values=c("blue", "gray", "red"))
```

# Add labels

```{r}
p + scale_colour_manual(values=c("blue", "gray", "red")) +
  labs(title="Gene Expression Changes Upon Drug Treatment",
       x="Control(no drug)", y="Drug Treatment")
```
